Operator: Good day, and welcome to the Pinnacle Asset Management Q3 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. As a reminder, the instructions on how to queue for questions will be given later. Please be advised that today's conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera: Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Pinnacle Asset Management's Q3 results. Joining me on today's call are Jane Hargrove, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Sarah Patel, Chief Investment Officer; and David Kwon, Head of Distribution.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that some of the statements made today may be forward-looking. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of the risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially.

With that, I'll turn the call over to Jane Hargrove.

Jane Hargrove: Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us. I'm pleased to report on our performance for Q3. We achieved solid results this quarter, driven by robust net inflows totaling $28.4 billion—our strongest quarterly inflow since Q4 2021. Our AUM grew to $728 billion.

Michael Chen: Thank you, Jane. From a financial perspective, Pinnacle Asset Management delivered strong results in Q3. Our revenue was $1.28 billion, representing an 18% increase year-over-year. This growth was primarily driven by a 22% increase in average AUM to $525 billion, fueled by those net inflows of $28.4 billion, particularly into our low-cost beta ETFs reminiscent of iShares and our alternatives platform, which attracted $6.2 billion in commitments amid strong limited partner interest in private credit given the higher-for-longer rate backdrop. Our expenses were managed prudently at $850 million, resulting in net income of $280 million. We continue to focus on operating leverage.

Good morning, everyone. Moving now to our key expense metrics, I'd like to provide some color on our compensation ratio, which came in at 42.1% for the third quarter, down 290 basis points year-over-year from 45.0% and 110 basis points sequentially from 43.2% in Q2. This marks our lowest quarterly ratio in over two years and reflects the strong operating leverage we've been building through revenue growth outpacing our disciplined approach to talent management and incentive alignment.

Compensation expense totaled $539 million, which includes base salaries, performance-based bonuses, long-term incentive plans or LTIPs, and equity-based awards. As a reminder, our comp structure is heavily variable—about 65% of total comp is performance-linked, tied directly to metrics like organic FUM growth, revenue per front-office professional, and risk-adjusted alpha generation across our active strategies.

Let me break this down further. Fixed compensation, which includes base salaries and benefits for our 4,200 global headcount, grew just 3% year-over-year to $185 million, reflecting modest merit increases of 2.5% for non-client-facing roles and targeted promotions in high-growth areas like ESG integration and quant trading desks. Variable comp, the bulk at $354 million, was down 5% from last year despite stronger results, as we leaned into deferral mechanisms—now 60% of bonuses are deferred into notional units tied to three-year TSR performance, with robust clawback provisions aligned with Dodd-Frank and our internal conduct policies. This helped compress the ratio even as we accrued for above-target payouts: front-office bonuses are pacing toward 120% of target, reflecting outperformance in our multi-asset credit strategies, which delivered 450 bps of excess return over benchmarks in a volatile fixed-income market reminiscent of the 2013 Taper Tantrum.

On trends, this 42.1% ratio is well below the industry peer average of 47% as reported in the latest Greenwich Associates survey for bulge-bracket managers like BlackRock and T. Rowe Price, and it's trending toward our medium-term target of 38-40%. Year-to-date, the ratio is 42.8%, a 320 bps improvement, largely from revenue acceleration: fee income from our passive ETF suite grew 25% on $10 billion in ETF inflows, benefiting from Vanguard-style cost compression—we're now at 7 bps average TER on core index products—while active equities held steady at 52 bps despite beta slippage in small-cap exposures. Headcount efficiency is another tailwind; revenue per employee hit $1.22 million, up from $1.05 million YoY, thanks to front-office stabilization after the 2022 talent wars.

Regionally, there's some nuance. In the Americas, which represent 55% of our AUM and 60% of comp expense, the ratio ticked up to 44% due to competitive pressures in New York and Toronto for portfolio managers specializing in alternatives—we hired 15 PMs from competitors like Apollo and KKR to bolster our $45 billion private markets platform, where dry powder deployment yielded 12% IRRs in Q3. EMEA came in leaner at 39%, aided by regulatory tailwinds from SFDR and AIFMD, allowing us to optimize back-office roles in London and Luxembourg with shared services. APAC was our efficiency standout at 37%, down from 41% YoY, as we shifted middle-office operations to our Singapore hub, leveraging lower labor costs and proximity to $120 billion in institutional mandates from sovereign wealth funds like GIC and Temasek, who are pivoting toward our thematic UCITS ETFs focused on Asia ex-Japan tech and renewables.

Strategically, we're embedding more tech-driven efficiencies to sustain this trajectory. Our $150 million investment in Aladdin-inspired portfolio optimization tools and GenAI for alpha research has reduced the need for junior analysts by 12% YoY, with natural attrition and upskilling programs redeploying talent to client coverage. We've also introduced comp scorecards linking 20% of LTIPs to non-financial KPIs like net promoter scores in wealth management—our RIA channel grew 15% to $80 billion—and carbon intensity reduction in public equities, aligning with client mandates from the likes of CalPERS. This isn't just cost control; it's about talent retention in a market where top quants command 20-30% premiums, as seen in recent moves at Citadel and Two Sigma.

Looking forward, we expect the full-year ratio to land at 42.5%, with Q4 potentially dipping below 41% on continued AUM momentum—assuming no major equity drawdown—and moderating variable accruals as we lap tough comps from 2022's bull market. Risks include talent poaching in a soft landing scenario or fee compression from active-to-passive shifts, but our multi-year comp framework, with 40% equity vesting over five years, ensures skin-in-the-game alignment with shareholder value creation. We're committed to GIPS-compliant transparency here, and I'll be happy to take questions on the comp appendix in our 10-Q.

I'll now turn to our total net flows, which came in at a robust $28.4 billion for the quarter—our strongest quarterly inflow since Q4 2021 and representing a 42% increase year-over-year from $20 billion in Q2 2023. This performance drove organic AUM growth of 2.8%, contributing to our total assets under management reaching $728 billion as of quarter-end, up 12% from year-end 2023.

To give you a clear picture, let me break this down by client channel, product suite, and region. By client channel, institutional flows were the standout at $18.2 billion in net inflows, accounting for 64% of the total. This was led by sovereign wealth funds and pension plans reallocating into our multi-asset solutions amid heightened market volatility, including two mandates totaling $4.5 billion from Middle Eastern SWFs drawn to our Pinnacle Global Alpha Fund, which has outperformed the MSCI World Index by 320 basis points over the past three years on a risk-adjusted basis. Retail and wealth management channels delivered $10.2 billion in net inflows, up 22% quarter-over-quarter, reflecting robust demand from high-net-worth individuals via our advisor network, bolstered by recent integrations with platforms like Envestnet and Orion Advisor Tech, expanding our reach to over 15,000 RIAs.

By product suite, our diversified mix resonated, with flows skewed toward defensive and income-oriented strategies amid persistent inflation concerns and the Fed's signaled rate cuts. ETFs generated $12.6 billion in net inflows—45% of total flows—driven by our Pinnacle Core Equity ETF (PINQ), which saw $3.2 billion alone, capturing share from Vanguard's equivalents thanks to its 0.08% expense ratio and active overlay tilts. Fixed income attracted $9.8 billion, up 35% YoY, as clients rotated into duration with the 10-year Treasury yield dipping to 4.2%; our Pinnacle Short Duration Credit Fund pulled in $2.1 billion with its AAA/AA-heavy portfolio and 5.2% yield-to-worst. Alternatives marked a milestone with $4.5 billion in inflows, a 60% YoY surge, fueled by our evergreen private credit interval fund launch, which closed at $1.8 billion AUM within weeks, outpacing peers in retail accessibility. Equities saw modest $1.5 billion net inflows, tempered by tactical outflows from cyclicals but offset by strength in thematic tech and healthcare.

Regionally, North America contributed $16.7 billion or 59% of total, resilient despite U.S. equity rotation risks. EMEA added $7.3 billion, led by UCITS-compliant ESG products up 28% YoY amid MiFID III and SFDR tailwinds, with traction in the UK defined contribution market. Asia-Pacific delivered $4.4 billion, our fastest-growing region at 55% YoY, propelled by onshore inflows into RMB-denominated funds via partnerships with ChinaAMC and Korea's NPS, capitalizing on yen carry unwinds and India's capex boom.

These flows underscore industry tailwinds like a flight to quality amid geopolitical tensions and U.S. election uncertainty, favoring our low-beta strategies; our 98.5% client retention rate, top decile per Morningstar; and market beta adding $45 billion in performance-related growth as long-only equity composites returned 8.2%, beating benchmarks by 150 bps. Our FlowOptix AI-driven flow analytics tool boosted conversion rates by 18%, and API integrations drove 25% of retail flows digitally. We're positioning for lower-for-longer rates with a $50 billion alternatives pipeline, including a GP stakes fund targeting 12-15% IRRs; ESG with our SustainCore ETF suite at $25 billion capturing 15% Article 8/9 share; and eyeing RIA custody M&A. We guide full-year net flows of $95-110 billion, implying 6-7% organic growth.

Sarah Patel: Thank you, Michael. On the investment front, we continue to focus on delivering strong risk-adjusted returns for our clients. Our key strategies performed well, particularly in fixed income and active equities. We are navigating the current market environment by leveraging our AI-enhanced portfolio construction platform and tactical positioning ahead of rate shifts. We launched our private credit interval fund this quarter, and the early reception has been positive, with $1.8 billion in AUM and strong institutional commitments.

I'll now turn to the drivers behind these impressive net flows, which totaled $28.4 billion and marked our strongest quarterly inflow since Q4 2021, a 28% increase year-over-year. This underscores the resilience of our franchise amid dynamic macro conditions, driven primarily by superior fund performance, favorable market tailwinds, and proactive product innovation.

Fund performance remains the largest driver, accounting for about 45% of net inflow attribution per our internal models. Our active equity strategies delivered exceptional alpha, with the Pinnacle Global Equity Fund outperforming the MSCI World Index by 420 basis points on a one-year basis net of fees, fueled by overweight mega-cap tech like NVIDIA and Broadcom amid the AI buildout, contributing over 60% of outperformance. In fixed income, our Core Bond Strategy captured 180 bps excess return versus the Bloomberg U.S. Aggregate, thanks to tactical duration extension ahead of the Fed's 50 bps September cut—our yield curve models signaled this in July.

Retail investors rewarded this with $4.2 billion into top-quartile funds per Morningstar, redemptions at just 2.1% of AUM versus industry 4.5%. Institutions added $6.8 billion, including a $1.5 billion European pension mandate attracted by our 1.42 Sharpe ratio in multi-asset solutions, ahead of peer median 1.05.

Market trends amplified this, contributing 35% to attribution. The S&P 500's 8.2% QoQ rally drew risk-on flows into our ETF suite; PinnacleSPY gathered $3.1 billion, capturing 15% active ETF share with smart-beta momentum and quality factors outperforming vanilla by 2-3% annualized. Private credit hit $2.9 billion record, our Direct Lending Fund at 9.8% yield, 450 bps over SOFR, appealing to RIAs shifting from high-yield bonds. Modest $800 million outflows from EM equity tied to China recovery issues, but EM ex-China like our $1.2 billion India Growth Fund shone amid 7%+ GDP.

Regionally, North America led with $7.6 billion (adjusted for total), via wirehouse strength and 98% advisor retention from tiered fees to 25 bps. EMEA $3.2 billion with 22% UCITS growth, 40% new AUM Article 8/9 per SFDR. APAC $1.6 billion at 45% YoY from HNW platforms into semis and renewables ETFs.

Strategically, our Q2-launched AI platform powers 70% of active strategies, optimizing factors and cutting tracking error to 1.5%, lifting outperforming calls to 78%. Five new active ETFs with $500 million seed target the $10 trillion ETF market at 12% CAGR. Digital funnel via Pinnacle Wealth portal generated 25% retail flows, conversions up 18%.

We see Q4 momentum with $25 billion RFP pipeline skewed to alts and multi-asset. Risks like yield repricing above 4.5%, but 15% low-vol positioning helps. Targeting 8-10% full-year flow margins with TER compression.

David Kwon: Thank you, Sarah. From a distribution perspective, we saw strong inflows into our ETF and alternatives funds. Our efforts to expand our reach in RIA and APAC channels are paying off, as evidenced by partnership-driven net inflows of $4.2 billion.

Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining our Q3 earnings call. Before diving deeper, I'd like to highlight our distribution partnerships and channel expansion efforts—one of our key growth drivers. In asset management, distribution fuels scalable AUM growth. We've advanced via a multi-channel strategy diversifying beyond wirehouses into RIAs, digital wealth managers, and international B2B2C, accelerating organic inflows and capturing share in a consolidating industry where top platforms control 60% of advisor flows per Cerulli.

In Q3, partnership-driven inflows hit $4.2 billion, 28% of total organics and up 35% YoY, lifting third-party AUM 12% QoQ to $185 billion—42% of our $440 billion platform average, outpacing industry's 38% per McKinsey. This is sticky, with 4.5-year tenure and 15% below-benchmark redemptions.

Success from three pillars: deepening partnerships, new channels, tech enablement. Deepening: Schwab's Advisor Services Apex Core Equity SMA suite saw $1.8 billion new deliveries, up 50% YoY via UMA sleeves on PortfolioCenter from our exclusive white-label. Fidelity Wealthscape drove $900 million to Apex Duration-Neutral Credit Fund, +120 bps over Aggregate. Morgan Stanley E*TRADE added APEX ESG ETF ($2.1 billion AUM, 0.18% ER) for $650 million, tapping $1.5 trillion ESG with 22% YTD ETF share. Merrill model marketplace at 65% penetration fueled $500 million into target-date series for $7 trillion DC/IRA at 5% CAGR.

Channel expansion: RIA/IBD now 55% U.S. advisor assets, growing 8%. Envestnet MoneyGuide/Tamarac integration unlocked $1.1 billion SMA from 1,200 RIAs via direct indexing with 45 bps tax-alpha. Europe: UBS advisor net scaled Apex Eurozone Equity to €1.2 billion, up 40%; Scalable Capital robo €450 million millennial flows. APAC: DBS Vickers SGD 800 million Asia ex-Japan; LatAm Itaú BRL 2.5 billion on reforms.

Tech: $25 million Distribution Tech Stack with Apex Connect APIs to Aladdin, Axys, Orion—onboarding to 10 days, conversions +22%. Piloting Securitize blockchain for fractional alts ($16T TAM).

Megatrends: models/direct indexing (35% new flows); embedded finance white-labels (18% retention lift); active-passive hybrids (4.2-star, 30% inflows). Expect $18 billion FY24 partnership flows, 25% up, 50% RIA/digital mix. Q4 launches: LPL IBD, Nomura Japan, BlackRock LifePath UMA. 95% renewal mitigates consolidation risks. ROA to 45 bps from 41.

Jane Hargrove: In summary, we are confident in our ability to continue delivering value to our shareholders. We are focused on executing our strategic priorities and capitalizing on the opportunities ahead. This includes accelerating organic growth, advancing tech transformation, deepening product innovation in alts and ESG, and expanding globally.

As we wrap up a strong quarter with AUM at $728 billion up 12% YoY on $28 billion net inflows, we're laser-focused on FY25 priorities built on four pillars: organic growth, tech transformation, product innovation emphasizing alternatives and ESG, and global footprint expansion.

Organic growth is north star: targeting 10-12% AUM to over $800 billion by FY25-end assuming 6-8% market appreciation. Net inflows $35-40 billion building on Q4 2.5% share in long-duration FI amid 75bps Fed cuts. Intensify institutional engagement with SWFs/pensions (15% RFP uptick); active equities +320bps S&P via mega-tech overweight. Retail models $4.2 billion flows, 22% millennial advisor growth. $150 million marketing converting $50 billion wirehouse to RIA.

Tech transformation: $250 million CapEx up 30% for Horizon AI platform—GenAI for optimization, scenarios, inflows modeling; pilots +15% Sharpe, blockchain T+1 saves 20bps on $200 billion ETFs. Alt data for ESG covering 98% $150 billion mandates, 25% edge vs Aladdin/Alpha.

Product innovation: Passive 45% AUM; ETF expansion incl. private credit interval 9-11% yields, semis thematic (25% CAGR), carbon transition ETF SFDR-compliant. Alts to $75 billion from $52 billion in direct lending/infra (200-300bps over HY); KKR co-mingled $10 billion UHNW. ESG $12 billion Q4 flows 35% total.

Global: NA 65%, APAC to 15% chasing $5T wealth transfer; 50 RMs Singapore/HK for 18% Asia ex-Japan fund. EMEA €20 billion DC via MiFID PRIIPs UCITS; EM India/Brazil 20%+ potential, $100 million JVs. Geopol stress-tests: 10% semis underweight.

Risk/talent: Climate VaR <5% drawdown, 150% liquidity; $80 million comp for 8% turnover, 45% women seniors.

These deliver 14-16% EPS growth, ROE 22%. Operator, open for questions.

Operator: Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs.

John Smith: Good morning. Can you provide more details on the drivers of your net flows this quarter?

Jane Hargrove: Thanks, John. As Sarah detailed, fund performance was key, with standout alpha in equities and fixed income driving 45% of attribution, alongside market rallies boosting ETFs and alts yield search. Regionally balanced, with tech overlays sustaining momentum—happy to dive deeper if needed.

John Smith: Thank you. And a follow-up on the compensation ratio improvement?

Michael Chen: Sure, John. The 42.1% reflects revenue outpacing variable comp via deferrals and efficiencies, below peers at 47%, trending to 38-40%. Regional nuances like APAC's 37% standout, tech reducing analysts 12%, sets up 42.5% full-year.

Operator: Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with Morgan Stanley.

Lisa Chen: Good morning. Could you elaborate on the performance of the Pinnacle Global Equity Fund?

Sarah Patel: Good morning, Lisa. The fund outperformed MSCI World by 420 bps net over one year, driven by 60%+ from AI mega-caps like NVIDIA. Sharpe strong, drawing $4.2 billion retail, institutional mandates—positioned well for continued tech infrastructure.

Lisa Chen: And how is the new private credit interval fund performing relative to expectations?

David Kwon: Thanks, Lisa. Early traction exceeded with $1.8 billion AUM quickly, record alts flows via partnerships like Schwab/Fidelity integrations. Yield appeal in higher rates, outpacing peers, with digital onboarding accelerating adoption.

Operator: Thank you. There are no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the call back over to Jane Hargrove for closing remarks.

Jane Hargrove: Thank you for joining us today. We appreciate your interest in Pinnacle Asset Management. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
